concept_summary: The same core loop as Distribution is the bottleneck, not the platform, rebuilt end to end for newcomers instead of its current crowd. Controls, difficulty, session shape, and rewards assume newcomers: a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners. Nothing in this build serves the old crowd; one client cannot satisfy both.
first_experiment: Take one level from the source fantasy, apply the inverted tuning only, and playtest with five target players for ten minutes; a quit-rate on the opposite side of half from the source baseline confirms the audience split is real.
source_idea_title: Distribution is the bottleneck, not the platform
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is tuned for its current crowd (Portal and search traffic.: systems tuned for veterans of the genre), this concept flips every tuning decision toward newcomers (a guided, jargon-free on-ramp for total beginners), so the two builds want mutually exclusive players.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Daily-ritual retention as the measured browser advantage stretched over a single persistent season lasting months: one meaningful decision per evening, no grinding, no catching up. Progress compounds across real calendar time and a missed week bends the story instead of ending it. The finale is scheduled, shared, and unrepeatable.
first_experiment: Concierge test: run the core decision by hand over seven daily messages with three players; if day-seven return beats the source's second-session return, the long form has legs.
source_idea_title: Daily-ritual retention as the measured browser advantage
why_it_is_opposite: While the source fits daily, this concept flips the clock: one season here outlasts hundreds of source sessions, so the source habit of quick payoff actively hurts.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Same-keyboard 2-player local duels as the growth category replanted on one shared map where every player acts at once and every move is visible. Resources, storms, and scarcities hit everyone simultaneously, so private optimization loses to public negotiation. The game only functions above fifty concurrent players.
first_experiment: Moderated crowd test: put fifteen volunteers on one shared board for twenty minutes; if alliances form without prompting, the social layer carries the game.
source_idea_title: Same-keyboard 2-player local duels as the growth category
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is a private experience, this concept flips it into a crowd: playing alone is impossible here, whereas the source never requires another person.
